title: Presheaf stalk of sectionwise extension of scalars
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $R_1,R_2$ sheaves of commutative rings, $\alpha:R_1\to R_2$ a morphism and $x\in X$. For each sheaf $F$ of $R_1$-modules, let $P_F$ be the presheaf of $R_2$-modules $U\mapsto R_2(U)\otimes_{R_1(U)}F(U)$ with tensor restrictions [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. There exists a family of $R_{2,x}$-linear isomorphisms $\Psi_F:R_{2,x}\otimes_{R_{1,x}}F_x\longrightarrow (P_F)_x$, where the scalar action is induced by $\alpha_x$ and stalks use [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], such that $\Psi_F(a_x\otimes s_x)=(a\otimes s)_x$ for every neighborhood $U$ of $x$, $a\in R_2(U)$ and $s\in F(U)$.

source.place: Tag 007K, label lemma-stalk-tensor-presheaf-modules; the source omits the proof, supplied here from varying-ring tensor colimits.

proof.text: For x in X, restrict the section ring presheaves and module presheaf to the directed poset of neighborhoods of x with reverse inclusion. Put A_U=R₁(U), M_U=R₂(U) with R₁(U)-action through α_U, N_U=F(U), and T_U=M_U tensor over A_U with N_U, the coefficient-first sectionwise change of rings of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Restrictions of M are semilinear by naturality of α, those of N by the presheaf module laws. The transition maps of T send pure tensors to tensors of restrictions. The colimit module actions are the stalk actions of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Their equations on coprojections are exactly the scalar action formula on germs.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-tensor-varying-rings] to these systems. Its bijective comparison ψ sends the germ of a coefficient-first pure tensor to the tensor of its two germs. The R₁,x-action on R₂,x is the action via α_x because α_x sends germ(r) to germ(α_U(r)). Thus the tensor carrier is precisely extension of scalars along α_x.

The comparison ψ is R₂,x-linear. For a scalar germ and a germ of a pure tensor choose representatives on one common neighborhood. Scalar multiplication on the section tensor multiplies its coefficient factor, and ψ sends that to multiplication on the stalk coefficient factor. Tensor induction proves this for any section tensor, and every stalk element has a section representative. Hence ψ and its inverse are R₂,x-linear. Invert ψ, regard the resulting linear equivalence as a ModuleCat isomorphism, and obtain the stated germ formula by applying the inverse to the equation for ψ. Choose these isomorphisms for every F; their germ formula determines them uniquely, since pure tensors generate and any pair of germs can be represented on a common neighborhood.

theorem stalkChangeOfRingsPresheafIso (X : TopCat.{u})
    (R₁ R₂ : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat.{u})
    (α : R₁ ⟶ R₂) (x : X) :
    ∃ Φ : ∀ F : SheafOfModules.{u}
        ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
          (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R₁),
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat x).map α.hom).hom).obj
        (ModuleCat.of (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := CommRingCat.{u}) (X := X) R₁.obj x)
          (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) (X := X) F.val.presheaf x)) ≅
      ModuleCat.of (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := CommRingCat.{u}) (X := X) R₂.obj x)
        (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) (X := X) (changeOfRingsPresheaf α F).presheaf x),
      (∀ (F : SheafOfModules.{u}
          ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
            (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R₁))
        (U : Opens X) (hx : x ∈ U) (s : F.val.obj (op U)) (a : R₂.obj.obj (op U)),
        (Φ F).hom
          (TopCat.Presheaf.germ (C := CommRingCat.{u}) (X := X) R₂.obj U x hx a
          ⊗ₜ[TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := CommRingCat.{u}) (X := X) R₁.obj x,
            ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat x).map α.hom).hom]
            TopCat.Presheaf.germ (C := Ab.{u}) (X := X) F.val.presheaf U x hx s) =
          TopCat.Presheaf.germ (C := Ab.{u}) (X := X) (changeOfRingsPresheaf α F).presheaf U x hx
            (a ⊗ₜ[R₁.obj.obj (op U), (α.hom.app (op U)).hom] s))
